title: Ukrainian drones knock out 36% of Russia's oil refining capacity in under two weeks
excerpt: Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out 36% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity in less than two weeks, hitting at least nine major refineries between Oct. 30 and Nov. 11, defense manufacturer Fire Point reported on Nov. 12.
content_html:
12 November, 02:08 PM

World

Smoke is rising in Leningrad Oblast after the drone attack, Nov. 11, 2026 (Photo: Social Media/via REUTERS)

Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out 36% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity in less than two weeks, hitting at least nine major refineries between Oct. 30 and Nov. 11, defense manufacturer Fire Point reported on Nov. 12.

The combined annual processing capacity of the Russian plants hit over the past 13 days exceeds 120 million metric tons of crude oil—accounting for 36% of the aggressor state’s entire domestic oil refining capacity.

"In under two weeks, enterprises accounting for more than a third of Russia's total oil refining capacity came under strike," Fire Point noted.

Recent Strikes on Russian Refineries

On Nov. 6, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that in direct retaliation for Russian strikes against Ukraine’s energy grid, Kyiv would press forward with its campaign targeting the aggressor state's oil refining infrastructure.

On Nov. 7, long-range drones struck Saratov Oil Refinery. Two days later, on Nov. 9, Ukrainian forces hit Russia's second-largest processing facility — Kirishi Oil Refinery in Leningrad Oblast.

On Nov. 11, strike drones hit oil export terminals at the Baltic port of Ust-Luga, a vital maritime hub for Russian crude shipments.

According to Reuters, Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries since late October 2026 have reduced Russia's operational refining capacity by roughly 30% and triggered acute fuel shortages across at least six Russian oblasts.
